label: Be a good coach
text: Give regular, specific, constructive feedback that balances praise with criticism, so people know what to keep doing and what to change. Hold frequent one-on-one meetings devoted to the employee's growth. Ask probing questions that pull insight out of the person rather than prescribing answers. Treat mistakes as coaching moments rather than occasions for blame.

label: Empower the team and do not micromanage
text: Give people real ownership of their work and the freedom to decide how to do it, staying available without hovering. Delegate meaningful decisions downward. Assign stretch work that grows people's capabilities. Judge by outcomes rather than controlling the process step by step.

label: Express interest in team members' success and personal well-being
text: Learn what motivates each person, what their life outside work looks like, and what they aspire to. Check in on people's welfare, not just their output. Make new hires feel genuinely welcomed and cared for as individuals.

label: Be productive and results-oriented
text: Help the team prioritize ruthlessly and focus energy on the work that matters most. Clear roadblocks that slow people down. Roll up your sleeves and do the work alongside the team when it counts. Hold everyone, including yourself, accountable for results.

label: Be a good communicator: listen and share information
text: Share context, goals, and reasoning openly so the team understands the why behind decisions. Create space for dissent and bad news. Listen carefully to concerns and close the loop so people know they were heard.

label: Help employees with career development
text: Have regular conversations with each person about where they want to grow. Help them set ambitious development goals, connect them with learning opportunities and mentors, and advocate for their advancement into new roles, even when it means losing a strong performer to another team.

label: Have a clear vision and strategy for the team
text: Articulate where the team is headed and why it matters. Translate that into concrete goals and priorities. Make sure every person understands how their own role contributes to the larger mission. Revisit and evolve the strategy with the team's input.

label: Have key technical skills to help advise the team
text: Keep enough technical skill to genuinely advise the team. Understand the craft of the work your people do. Dig into hard problems alongside them. Give guidance grounded in real knowledge of the domain rather than generic platitudes.

label: I know what is expected of me at work
text: I know what is expected of me at work: my role, my responsibilities, and what good performance looks like are clearly defined, and my manager has made sure I understand them.

label: I have the materials and equipment I need to do my work right
text: I have the materials, equipment, tools, budget, and resources I need to do my work right, without constantly fighting broken systems or missing basics.

label: At work, I have the opportunity to do what I do best every day
text: My role is built around my strengths: most days I get to do the things I am naturally good at and energized by, rather than grinding through work that fits someone else.

label: In the last seven days, I have received recognition or praise for doing good work
text: In the last seven days, someone noticed my good work and said so: I received specific recognition or praise for something I did well, not just silence or criticism.

label: My supervisor, or someone at work, seems to care about me as a person
text: My supervisor, or someone at work, seems to care about me as a person: they take an interest in my well-being and my life, not just my output.

label: There is someone at work who encourages my development
text: There is someone at work who encourages my development: a person who pushes me to grow, learn new skills, and take on bigger challenges.

label: At work, my opinions seem to count
text: At work, my opinions seem to count: when I raise a concern or suggest an idea, people listen and it can actually change decisions.

label: The mission or purpose of my company makes me feel my job is important
text: The mission and purpose of my company make me feel my job is important: I can see how my daily work connects to something meaningful.

label: My associates or fellow employees are committed to doing quality work
text: My teammates are committed to doing quality work: the people around me take pride in doing things well and hold high standards.

label: I have a best friend at work
text: I have a genuine friend at work: someone I trust, enjoy spending time with, and can be honest with beyond task talk.

label: In the last six months, someone at work has talked to me about my progress
text: In the last six months, someone at work has sat down with me to talk about my progress: how I am doing, what is improving, and where I should focus next.

label: This last year, I have had opportunities at work to learn and grow
text: This last year I have had real opportunities to learn and grow at work: new skills, new responsibilities, training, or experiences that stretched me.
